articles.title: Help EFF Solve an Issue That's Bigger than Creepy Ads
articles.summary: Microsoft drops 167 vulns including a SharePoint zero-day and Windows Defender's 'BlueHammer' flaw. Meanwhile Chrome notches its fourth zero-day of the year because apparently they're collecting them like Pokemon cards.

articles.title: Malware crew TeamPCP open-sources its Shai-Hulud worm on GitHub
articles.summary: Mystery leaker 'YellowKey' keeps gifting the world fresh Microsoft zero-days like a deranged security Santa. Their latest makes stolen laptops infinitely more terrifying.

articles.title: maru-deep-pro-search 0.9.3
articles.summary: Google catches the first AI-generated zero-day in the wild, proving our robot overlords have learned to hack before they learned to love. Threat actors are now outsourcing exploit dev to ChatGPT's evil twin.

articles.title: Anti-DDoS Firm Heaped Attacks on Brazilian ISPs
articles.summary: Canvas gets pwned harder than a freshman's first CS assignment, disrupting schools nationwide. Cybercriminals defaced login pages with ransom demands because apparently holding education hostage is the new black.

articles.title: Microsoft's MDASH AI System Finds 16 Windows Flaws Fixed in Patch Tuesday
articles.summary: Foxconn confirms breach after ransomware crew claims to have stolen Apple and Nvidia's crown jewels. Nothing says 'supply chain security' like your manufacturer getting absolutely rekt.

articles.title: Victory! End-to-End Encrypted RCS Comes to Apple and Android Chats
articles.summary: Instagram kills its barely-used end-to-end encryption feature, breaking years-old promises. Meta continues its proud tradition of saying one thing about privacy while doing absolutely nothing.

articles.title: EFF Launches New Offline Campaign for Saudi Wikipedian Osama Khalid
articles.summary: Victory! iPhone-Android RCS chats finally get end-to-end encryption by default. Only took Apple approximately forever to stop treating cross-platform privacy like a competitive disadvantage.

articles.title: Dark Reading Celebrates 20 Years as a Leading Authority on Cybersecurity, Highlighting the People, Events, Ideas, and Technologies Shaping the Modern Risk Landscape
articles.summary: EFF launches campaign for Saudi Wikipedian Osama Khalid, imprisoned for the radical act of contributing to open knowledge. Turns out authoritarian regimes really hate people who make information free.

articles.title: Patch Tuesday, April 2026 Edition
articles.summary: Scattered Spider's 'Tylerb' pleads guilty to wire fraud and aggravated identity theft after a 2022 SMS phishing spree. Another social engineering savant trades lulz for federal time.

articles.title: California colleges went big on online learning tools. Then the worst happened
articles.summary: Fortinet drops critical RCE patches for FortiSandbox and FortiAuthenticator because irony is dead and security appliances are the new attack vector du jour.
